nodes.label: index.html — portfolio page
nodes.rationale: Single page carrying the markup, the static hero, the noscript fallbacks and the JSON-LD; dark colour-scheme, self-hosted type, six numbered sections from Projects to Contact.

nodes.label: Static hero markup (hero-title, pre-JS)
nodes.rationale: js/render.js overwrites the title and stat strip from js/data.js, but they are written out statically too because an empty hero is what actually caused layout shift. Matching the static markup to the rendered output removes the shift at its source and gives a scriptless reader the real headline.

nodes.label: Hero stat strip (systems, yearly benefit, cash, agency quote, salary payback)
noscript project fallback (scriptless build list)
nodes.rationale: Crawlers and scriptless readers get every build in text with the same measured figures the cards show. These drifted two measurement rounds behind once and nobody noticed, because nothing renders them on a normal load.

nodes.label: noscript engineering-notes fallback
nodes.rationale: Same contract as the project grid — the argument survives without JavaScript, in short form, kept in step with HARD_PARTS.

nodes.label: JSON-LD entity markup (Person + ItemList of SoftwareApplication)
nodes.rationale: Mirrors js/data.js and is now guarded by npm run check, because it is read by crawlers and never by the browser — it had already lost a project and carried a reworded description with nothing on a normal load showing it was wrong. Deliberately carries no rating, price or date that is not in the source data.

nodes.label: render-warning banner (role=alert)
nodes.rationale: Tells the reader the visible text is the stored fallback and may be out of date, and points at an email address for current numbers, instead of silently presenting stale figures as current.

nodes.label: Project sort radiogroup (featured / cost avoided / build time)
nodes.rationale: Radiogroup with a labelled sort control and an sr-only aria-live status region so the reordering is announced to screen readers.

nodes.label: What each tool replaced — comparison table
nodes.rationale: Before/after process, hours reclaimed and monthly worth, with a footnote stating contract estimates are a judgement priced at a US contract rate, not a quote received.

nodes.label: What it costs to run — token cost breakdown
nodes.rationale: Every retained assistant turn on the machine priced at published API list rates per model, alongside two explicit comparisons and a caveat line.

nodes.label: How these numbers were made — method and honesty section
nodes.rationale: Publishes the derivation, the failure of the previous hand count, the guard that enforces consistency, and the system deliberately excluded — so no figure has to be taken on trust.

nodes.label: npm run measure provenance note
nodes.rationale: Line counts come from git ls-files so dependencies, build output and untracked scratch are excluded by construction; test counts are what each runner reports because tests passing should mean the tests were run; cost comes from 551 Claude Code transcripts, a floor rather than a lifetime total since old transcripts are pruned. The earlier hand count could not be reproduced — twenty-four candidate rules reproduced no more than one of the six figures, each had been counted to a different boundary, and the script found a notes vault committed inside a repo, a generated 1,911-line runtime file copied into three projects, and a page committed twice under two names.

nodes.label: Sixth system omitted on purpose (OIS connectors)
nodes.rationale: The source document counts six systems and a $30,748 base case; the page shows five and $28,162 because the OIS connectors and canonical data model were never finished and are used by two people. Dropping it costs $2,586 and takes the headline from 102% to 94%. Every total is summed from the systems actually shown; nothing retypes the source total.

nodes.label: Self-hosted type with two preloaded faces
nodes.rationale: The hero headline and the mono kicker above it are the first text painted, so those two faces are preloaded rather than waiting on the stylesheet to be parsed.

nodes.label: No image preload — the LCP element is the h1
nodes.rationale: The measured LCP element is the h1 at every breakpoint, so preloading a card screenshot would only compete with the font and stylesheet fetches that actually gate first paint.

nodes.label: Skip-to-projects link
Juan J Garibay (Person entity)
nodes.rationale: Solo builder at Tr3s del Valle who ships production internal tools with AI-assisted development, publishing build time, cost and test-count evidence for each one.

nodes.label: Tr3s del Valle (Organization)
nodes.rationale: The food distribution business these internal tools actually run.

nodes.label: Rutero TDV — route operations
nodes.rationale: Route planning, driver dispatch and field-sales prospecting for a real distribution fleet. Sits behind a login and shows the customer master, which is why it has no public demo recording.

nodes.label: Cotizador TDV v8 — logistics quoting
nodes.rationale: Generates priced logistics quotes and exports them straight to PDF.

nodes.label: Data Triage Center — catalogue triage
nodes.rationale: Cleans product catalogue rows and validates UPCs one keystroke at a time; the only listed build with no public URL.

nodes.label: TDV Outbound Log — shipment logging
nodes.rationale: Scans and logs outbound shipments against a barcode-indexed catalogue.

nodes.label: Cotizador Farmers Fresh — second quoting engine
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt from scratch for a different importer and its lanes rather than parameterising the first quoting engine. Its access control is still disabled, so it is not safe to record for a public demo.

nodes.label: Currents — swipe-driven learning PWA
nodes.rationale: Installs to a phone home screen and works offline. The only consumer build here and the only one holding no business data, which is why it carries the site's single demo recording.

nodes.label: Hard part — a delivery confirmed with no signal
nodes.rationale: A driver marks an order delivered in a dead zone and the phone retries later, by which time the office may have reopened it. Every close is conditioned on the row version the driver saw, so a repeat matches nothing and a stale close is dropped (supabase/migrations/20260814060000_orders_write_discipline.sql).

nodes.label: Hard part — several reps, one shared phone
nodes.rationale: The first version treated 'gone from the queue' as 'safely delivered' and destroyed the only proof a visit happened. Queued changes now carry their owner and are re-read at the moment of sending (app/src/services/visitSync.ts).

nodes.label: Hard part — widening one permission opened a door
nodes.rationale: Giving drivers all six territories meant a stolen login could erase another rep's visit and sign it as theirs; a trigger restores the original author on any non-admin attempt to change it (supabase/migrations/20260813180000_visit_author_and_photo_owner_hardening.sql).

nodes.label: Hard part — splitting one truck's freight fairly
nodes.rationale: Two legs, two currencies, and products that ride only part of the way. Two independent cost pools divided by units, cases, weight or value, with manual overrides layered on top so one line cannot move the pool under the others.

nodes.label: Hard part — a barcode a cheap scanner will read
nodes.rationale: A hand-written Code 128 encoder with no library, plus a self-test that measures the bars back out of the drawing and decodes them, checking the checksum and that the text matches the product code that went in (verify-barcodes.js).

nodes.label: Hard part — a barcode can be valid and still be wrong
nodes.rationale: Check-digit maths across four formats, plus collision checks against both the live sheet and the unsaved edit queue, and brand-prefix cross-referencing (catalog-logic.js).

nodes.label: Hard part — knowing what day it is on someone else's phone
nodes.rationale: A UTC timestamp stamps an evening session in Mexico with tomorrow's date. Day keys are built from local calendar fields; differences are read as UTC midnights so the count is exact across a clock change (src/lib/streak.js).
